clue.text: Do something magical that changes all aspects

indicators.note: the words all aspects are changed, their letters rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A wizard's trick that transforms every side of something at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that changes' rearranges ALL ASPECTS into the three-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To work a spell or enchantment is the idiomatic way of saying someone has done magic.

clue.text: Stop up in Irish city

definitions.meaning: to plug or seal a bottle with a stopper
the large port city in the south of the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck, or holed up, in a town in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a bung of bark plugs a bottle, and the place is Ireland's second city.

clue.text: Mark half of internal passage?

parts.note: semi- is a prefix meaning half
the colon is part of the large intestine, a passage inside the body

explanation.surface: Pointing out half of some passage inside a building or body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is the punctuation mark; the question mark flags the anatomical reading of 'internal passage'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a punctuation symbol, a dot over a comma, used between clauses.

clue.text: Minister losing head in criminal act

indicators.note: losing head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A clergyman is beheaded in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a serious crime, a criminal act.

clue.text: Left time to make payment for carrying goods

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Taking a break and leaving it a while before paying a delivery bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is the charge made for carriage, the cost of transporting goods.

clue.text: See bounder having a grip on the heartless set

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: having a grip on means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a cad is a bounder, an ill-mannered man

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed

explanation.surface: Look at a rogue clutching a heartless gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the H from THE, leaving TE, which CAD grips.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set in a place is situated there, its position fixed.

clue.text: Track used by top athletes

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A running track that the best athletes train on.
explanation.definitionFit: A track is a narrow way or trail for walking, a synonym.

clue.text: Insects sat on by a girl

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sat on by another has that other piece placed above it

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Bugs being sat on by a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name, given as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Shopping thoroughfare? You could get tights here

indicators.note: could get suggests the words tights and here can be reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The main shopping street is where you could buy tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get' rearranges TIGHTS and HERE; the surface is also true, since shops on the main street sell hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the main street of a town, lined with shops, is the shopping street.

clue.text: Twin reveals birds by river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: A twin shows off some birds beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend the founders of Rome were twin brothers, and he was Romulus's twin.

clue.text: Tying up again with string or tape?

definitions.meaning: re- means again and cording means binding with cord or string
a tape holds a sound or video record of something

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to tie a parcel again with string or with tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tape' looks like an alternative to string for tying, but it is the cassette sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-cording is binding with cord again, and a tape is a sound or video record.

clue.text: Free from obligation and religion, not half, naughty woman!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word religion is kept, its first four letters

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, who disobeyed by eating the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: Someone renouncing duty and half their faith, with a cheeky exclamation at a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a duty is to release them from it.

clue.text: Conservative diplomacy in meeting

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for a Conservative in British politics
tact is diplomacy, skill in handling people

explanation.surface: A Tory shows diplomatic skill at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact is coming together or touching, a synonym for a meeting.

clue.text: City feels great pity when bishop goes

indicators.note: goes means that letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: to bleed for someone is to feel deep sympathy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A city feels deep sorrow at its bishop's departure.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in Yorkshire, northern England, given as an example of a city.

clue.text: First lady to make a song and dance?

definitions.text: to make a song and dance?
definitions.note: describes a person, a temperamental one given to making a fuss, so the noun fits

parts.note: prima is Italian for first
donna is Italian for lady

explanation.surface: A first lady making a great fuss, or performing on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'make a song and dance' is a British idiom for making a needless fuss, which a temperamental star is known for.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading female opera singer, often vain and temperamental, prone to fussing over little things.

clue.text: Little relative somewhere in church being ill again?

parts.note: rel is a shortened form of relative
the apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: A young relation is unwell again somewhere in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling back into illness after a recovery is the medical sense of the word.

clue.text: Gas for energy brought across hollow in the ground

indicators.note: brought across means taken over to sit beside the hollow

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a pan is a natural basin or depression in the ground
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gas for producing power is piped over a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hydrocarbon gas used as a fuel in cylinders.

clue.text: Item of furniture for one who has just got up?

definitions.meaning: a kitchen sideboard with shelves for plates

definitions.text: one who has just got up?
definitions.meaning: got up means dressed, so this is a person who has put on clothes

explanation.surface: Choosing furniture for someone who has just risen from bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' suggests rising from bed, but here it means clothed, as in a fancy get-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen cabinet with shelves, and literally a person who puts clothes on.

clue.text: Really great guy working in our sphere

indicators.note: working suggests the words our sphere are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wonderful fellow operating in our circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges OUR SPHERE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic-book hero with powers is, jokingly, an exceptionally great man.

clue.text: Sun about to go? Here's the wind and rain

definitions.text: Sun about to go? Here's the wind and rain

parts.words: Sun about to go? Here's the wind and rain
parts.note: Sun is Sunday: when Sunday is about to go, Mon(day) is coming soon, and the weather is a seasonal storm

explanation.surface: The sunshine is ending and bad weather is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is the abbreviation for Sunday, not the star: when Sunday ends, Mon is soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal wind of South Asia, bringing heavy rain, is the wind and rain described.

clue.text: It could be a clue for ones to detect

parts.note: taking the word nose with out as an anagram signal gives the letters of ones, so the phrase is a clue for ones

explanation.surface: Something might serve as a hint for people trying to find things.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: NOSE with OUT as an anagram signal makes ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sniff out or discover something by searching is the idiomatic sense here.

clue.text: Expensive article in Paris — riders raced to get to one

definitions.text: riders raced to get to one

parts.note: steep is informal for overpriced
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: A costly item in Paris, with jockeys racing to reach it.
explanation.walkthrough: Steeplechases were first run across country towards a church tower as the finishing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Early horse races were run from church spire to church spire, hence the steeplechase.

clue.text: Observed absorbing short NT book in drinking den

indicators.note: absorbing means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: seen means observed
Heb is the abbreviation for the Epistle to the Hebrews in the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone is seen reading a small Bible in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking house is an illicit bar or den.

clue.text: Short drink — then there's a turbulent episode

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, a short

explanation.surface: A quick whisky leads to a stormy scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or emotional sequence of events, a turbulent episode.

clue.text: Notice US university offering welcome?

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An American university advertises that it is welcoming applicants.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, to receive or welcome them.

clue.text: Vessel discharged mates to meet the Queen

indicators.note: discharged suggests the word mates is let loose and rearranged

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A ship's crew, released from duty, meets the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a vessel powered by steam.

clue.text: End being upset when a female joins in criminal gang

indicators.note: joins in means those letters are placed inside the other piece
in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Things come to a messy end when a woman joins a crime syndicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns AIM into MIA; 'joins in' puts A and F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian or American crime organisation is the archetypal criminal gang.

clue.text: Some frothy persuasiveness put into his?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A salesman pumps some frothy talk into his pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a promoter's pitch: excited publicity is what he puts into his patter.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated promotional talk is what a salesman injects into his spiel.

clue.text: Boss as individual with less feeling

parts.note: number here is the comparative of numb, having less sensation
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A boss is a person with less feeling than others.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge is colloquially called the top man, the chief.

clue.text: Angry word of disapproval delivered to railway

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: An irate complaint is sent to the railway company.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery temper is a hot, passionate, angry one.

clue.text: Agreements to exclude piano performances

indicators.note: to exclude means that letter is left out of the word

parts.note: pacts are agreements or treaties
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Contracts are drawn up to bar the pianist from the shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts are the separate turns or routines in a variety show.

clue.text: Old nana set to suffer without extra support

indicators.note: suffer suggests the words old nana set are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly grandmother is going to struggle without more help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffer' rearranges OLD NANA SET; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something self-contained operates independently, needing no outside help.
